system_description.narrative_title: Multipolar Strain: Wars, Protests, Markets and Tech Frictions
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system under simultaneous stress from regional wars (Ukraine, Middle East proxy clashes), disruptive great‑power competition (US‑China‑Russia), and a cascade of domestic political shocks (mass protests and volatile elections in France, Brazil, Serbia, Israel). Economic and technological linkages — energy and commodity markets, higher yields and central‑bank policy, and space/communications infrastructure like Starlink — transmit and amplify shocks, producing rapid feedbacks across regions and sectors. These overlapping dynamics make policy tradeoffs more fraught and increase the chance of spillovers and unintended escalation.
system_description.scope: Interstate security dynamics (conventional and proxy conflicts), great‑power strategic competition, regional security complexes (Middle East, Eastern Europe), global financial markets and central‑bank policy, critical supply chains (energy, rare earths), transnational technology/space/cyber infrastructure, and major domestic political processes (protests, elections).
system_description.super_system: The global political‑economic and environmental system: an interconnected international order of states, markets, information/technology networks, and planetary resource/climate constraints.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain at war with shifting frontlines, episodic local ceasefires and persistent strikes on logistics and civilian infrastructure.

variables.name: U.S.–Iran regional confrontation
variables.description: The United States and Iran, through direct and proxy actions (including Houthi attacks), are locked in an escalating Middle East confrontation threatening Gulf ports, airfields and maritime routes.

variables.name: China's supply‑chain and grey‑zone pressure
variables.description: China is tightening control over strategic supply chains and employing grey‑zone pressure against regional rivals—notably Japan and Taiwan—to convert economic leverage into geopolitical gains.

variables.name: Global financial and bond‑market shock
variables.description: Eurozone and Asian central banks and global investors are grappling with elevated bond‑market volatility, deepening yield shocks and policy uncertainty that are reconfiguring capital flows.

variables.name: Wave of protests and electoral upheaval
variables.description: A transnational wave of mass protests and pivotal elections—from France and Brazil to Serbia and Israel—is reshaping domestic power structures and populist political alignments.
